text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] realtime-api: p99 latency = 3.1s (SLO 2.0s) over last 6m. Triggered 2026-03-17T09:15:01Z. Paging oncall.

devin: oncall here, paging acknowledged. starting quick triage.

amelia: i'm online, pulling grafana dashboards now -> https://grafana.internal/redwood/realtime-api/p99

devin: quick check: `sum(rate(request_duration_seconds{route=\"/v1/realtime\"}[$__range]))` looks elevated on eu-west.

raj: I'm paged, taking the handoff. ping if you need me to run anything on nodes.

luis: seeing a spike in streaming-tail latency and a simultaneous jump in kvcache miss rate in eu-west. recent metrics: kvcache_miss_rate 78% -> 80% @09:12.

jenny: CS: no mass customer tickets yet, but one enterprise reported slow streaming completions ~20m ago. no errors, just timeouts on client-side at ~5s.

caroline: product: embeddings background jobs also show elevated p95. probably related but might be different route.

raj: running a quick curl against a busy realtime host to measure tail.
```
# on bastion
$ time curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}s" https://realtime-eu-west-03.redwood.internal/health
3.52s
```

ops-bot: autoscaling action: scaled realtime-eu-west pool +2 replicas at 2026-03-17T09:20:14Z.

amelia: I pushed a temporary routing override to shift 25% traffic from eu-west to eu-backup-pool. command: `redwood route set --route realtime-api --percent 25 --from eu-west --to eu-backup-pool`

luis: looking at deploys: there was a config rollout earlier (08:50) that adjusted kvcache.size from 64MB -> 16MB on the realtime model-worker. commit: a1b2c3d. that could explain miss spike and tail.

devin: can we validate by reverting config on a canary? small rollback on one host to 64MB and watch p99.

raj: initiating canary rollback on node realtime-03-eu.
```
# config rollback
$ kubectl patch deploy realtime-worker --namespace=eu-west --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","env":[{"name":"KVCACHE_SIZE_MB","value":"64"}]}]}}}}'
```

incident-bot: canary update applied to realtime-03-eu at 2026-03-17T09:23:05Z. Monitoring p99 on that host.

amelia: on grafana the canary host p99 dropped to 1.85s within 45s of rollback. overall eu-west p99 trending down but still above SLO at cluster level.

ops-bot: routing adjustment increased to 40% failover to backup pool to reduce customer impact.

luis: confirming recent changes look like the root cause: aggressive kvcache reduction under pressure -> higher miss rate -> more regen + tail latency. will add as suspected root cause for follow-up.

raj: promoting config rollback cluster-wide after canary stability (rolling restart scheduled).

incident-bot: global p99 now 1.92s 2m after cluster rollback. SLO restored.

jenny: CS: I'll open a high-priority note for the enterprise that reported slowness and flag as degraded performance window 09:05-09:25 UTC.

caroline: drafting customer communication for impacted customers, will post to #customer-notify once reviewed by leadership.

amelia: action items: 1) revert kvcache sizing change from earlier rollout 2) add regression test in canary suite to prevent kvcache reductions without load-profile validation 3) postmortem and timeline.

raj: rolling restart completed at 09:28, all nodes back to KVCACHE_SIZE_MB=64. monitoring 10m.

devin: handing back to oncall rotation: i'll keep monitoring for 30m then close the page if stable. thanks all. :thumbsup: 

caroline: noted for postmortem and customer comms.

luis: i'll file a follow-up ticket to add telemetry alert for sudden kvcache_miss_rate > 50% so we catch this earlier.

ops-bot: mitigation actions recorded: scaled replicas, route shift, canary rollback, cluster rollback.

raj: handing off to devin for monitoring. handoff complete.

devin: acknowledged, keeping watch. will escalate if p99 >2.0s again. closing page if stable after window.
